claims: The Ivy League consists of eight private universities in the Northeastern United States.
The Ivy League was originally formed as an athletic conference in 1954.
The Ivy League schools are Brown, Columbia, Cornell, Dartmouth, Harvard, Princeton, University of Pennsylvania, and Yale.
Brown University is in Providence, RI.
Columbia University is in New York City, NY.
Cornell University is in Ithaca, NY.
Dartmouth College is in Hanover, NH.
Harvard University is in Cambridge, MA.
Princeton University is in Princeton, NJ.
University of Pennsylvania is in Philadelphia, PA.
Yale University is in New Haven, CT.
Acceptance rates for Ivy League institutions often fall below 5-8% for top candidates, according to data for the Class of 2028/2029.
Most Ivy League schools were founded before the US Declaration of Independence.
Cornell was not founded before the US Declaration of Independence.
Ivy League schools compete against each other in NCAA Division I
